questions.question: What is the primary purpose of automation in Cortex security operations?
options: To replace all analyst review with unsupervised actions
To streamline and optimize security operations tasks through automated workflows
To disable manual investigation tools during case response
To store marketplace content outside the Cortex platform
correct_answers: To streamline and optimize security operations tasks through automated workflows

questions.question: In a typical Cortex automation workflow, what happens after an issue triggers a playbook?
options: The playbook executes predefined tasks as part of the response workflow
All issue fields are deleted before analysis begins
The Marketplace automatically reverts installed content packs
The case is closed without logging any actions
correct_answers: The playbook executes predefined tasks as part of the response workflow

questions.question: Which component is described as the core automation engine within Cortex?
options: Dashboards
Playbooks
Reports
Version History
correct_answers: Playbooks

questions.question: Which two Cortex components are specifically associated with extracting, manipulating, and presenting data in JSON format?
options: Filters
Transformers
Dashboards
Case layouts
correct_answers: Filters
Transformers

questions.question: How does automation help reduce issue fatigue?
options: By automating initial triage and categorization so analysts can prioritize high-priority cases
By increasing the number of duplicate issues analysts must review
By preventing all integrations from triggering events
By removing all manual escalation paths
correct_answers: By automating initial triage and categorization so analysts can prioritize high-priority cases

questions.question: What is the Cortex Marketplace primarily used for?
options: Managing content packs that enhance operations with playbooks, integrations, scripts, and related content
Running endpoint scans without installed content
Replacing the case War Room with a reporting dashboard
Storing local-only scripts outside Cortex
correct_answers: Managing content packs that enhance operations with playbooks, integrations, scripts, and related content

questions.question: Which product is associated with the full Cortex Marketplace experience in the lesson's comparison table?
options: Cortex XSIAM
Cortex Cloud only
Cortex XDR only
Any product using Lite Experience
correct_answers: Cortex XSIAM

questions.question: Why should users review details before installing a content pack?
options: To examine content, dependencies, version history, and reviews before adding it to the Cart
To permanently detach all scripts from their content packs
To prevent content packs from receiving future updates
To force all optional dependencies to install silently
correct_answers: To examine content, dependencies, version history, and reviews before adding it to the Cart

questions.question: What is true about content pack updates in the Marketplace?
options: Updates are not installed automatically and administrators manually initiate the update process
Updates always delete user customizations
Updates can only be performed by opening the War Room
Updates are available only for Lite Experience products
correct_answers: Updates are not installed automatically and administrators manually initiate the update process

questions.question: What is the consequence of detaching a script from its Marketplace content pack?
options: The script can be modified, but it no longer receives updates from that content pack
The script becomes permanently disabled and cannot be duplicated
The script is automatically converted to a dashboard widget
The script loses access to all command arguments
correct_answers: The script can be modified, but it no longer receives updates from that content pack

questions.question: What is the main goal of Automation Features in Cortex?
options: To simplify repetitive tasks and enable predefined responses to specific SOC triggers
To remove all playbooks from case management
To require separate setup screens for every automation action
To replace issue-level automation with only manual tasks
correct_answers: To simplify repetitive tasks and enable predefined responses to specific SOC triggers

questions.question: Automation Features operate primarily at which level?
options: Issue level
Global license level
Dashboard widget level
Archive storage level
correct_answers: Issue level

questions.question: What does the no-context-switching design help analysts do?
options: Build automations, connect integrations, and create rules from the same workflow area
Disable all rules when opening the playbook editor
Move every automation task into the Settings menu
Prevent playbooks from using integration instances
correct_answers: Build automations, connect integrations, and create rules from the same workflow area

questions.question: Why can the playbook catalog show different playbooks across XSIAM, XDR, and Cortex Cloud tenants?
options: Playbook availability varies by product and compatible content is shown for that platform
Only manually created playbooks are allowed in XSIAM
XDR and Cortex Cloud always show more Marketplace content than XSIAM
The catalog hides all adopted playbooks by design
correct_answers: Playbook availability varies by product and compatible content is shown for that platform

questions.question: What happens when an out-of-the-box playbook is adopted?
options: Its underlying Marketplace content pack is installed in the background
It is deleted from the catalog
It becomes editable without duplication
It can no longer be enabled or disabled
correct_answers: Its underlying Marketplace content pack is installed in the background

questions.question: Why must an out-of-the-box playbook be duplicated before modification?
options: The original template is locked to preserve its integrity
Duplicating permanently disables the original playbook
Duplicating is required only for manual tasks
The duplicate removes all task inputs
correct_answers: The original template is locked to preserve its integrity

questions.question: Which trigger type is best suited for immediate response when new issues meet defined criteria?
options: Issue-based trigger
Feed-based job trigger
Version history trigger
Manual list import
correct_answers: Issue-based trigger

questions.question: How are jobs different from automation rules in Automation Features?
options: Jobs follow a proactive scheduled or feed-driven approach, while automation rules are typically reactive
Jobs can only run manually from a case view
Jobs cannot execute playbooks
Jobs are used only to delete integration instances
correct_answers: Jobs follow a proactive scheduled or feed-driven approach, while automation rules are typically reactive

questions.question: What are Quick Actions designed for?
options: Fast, repetitive, single-command automations that do not require full playbook logic
Large multi-issue workflows that always require complex branching
Replacing integrations with static reports
Creating content pack version histories
correct_answers: Fast, repetitive, single-command automations that do not require full playbook logic

questions.question: From where can an analyst manually launch a Quick Action according to the lesson?
options: By right-clicking an issue in the Issues table and selecting Run Automation
Only from the Marketplace Browse tab
Only from the license management screen
By editing the system health chart panel
correct_answers: By right-clicking an issue in the Issues table and selecting Run Automation

questions.question: What is the purpose of jobs in Cortex?
options: To execute playbooks in response to specific events or time triggers
To prevent recurring automation from running
To replace playbooks with static lists
To remove all job status information from the interface
correct_answers: To execute playbooks in response to specific events or time triggers

questions.question: Which two job types are described in the lesson?
options: Time-triggered jobs
Feed-triggered jobs
Dashboard-triggered jobs
License-triggered jobs
correct_answers: Time-triggered jobs
Feed-triggered jobs

questions.question: When should a time-triggered job be used?
options: When tasks need to run at a predetermined time or regular interval
Only when a feed changes unexpectedly
Only when an analyst manually opens a War Room
When a content pack must be deleted
correct_answers: When tasks need to run at a predetermined time or regular interval

questions.question: What causes a feed-triggered job to execute?
options: Changes or updates in all feeds or selected feeds
A user opening the version history of a list
A dashboard widget exceeding its width
A playbook task being marked manual
correct_answers: Changes or updates in all feeds or selected feeds

questions.question: Which job use case is best suited for monitoring a vulnerability feed and running remediation when new vulnerabilities appear?
options: A feed-triggered vulnerability management job
A manual communication task
A list version rollback
A content pack deletion action
correct_answers: A feed-triggered vulnerability management job

questions.question: What information can be checked from the Jobs page views?
options: Job status, last run, next run, and additional details
Only content pack user reviews
Only case layout rules
Only endpoint isolation status
correct_answers: Job status, last run, next run, and additional details

questions.question: What does the Jobs page Chart Panel display?
options: Counts of jobs by states and trigger types, such as running, waiting, error, disabled, time triggered, and event triggered
Only the raw JSON output of the selected job
Only a list of installed Marketplace integrations
Only command-line help for list commands
correct_answers: Counts of jobs by states and trigger types, such as running, waiting, error, disabled, time triggered, and event triggered

questions.question: What does the Disable job action do?
options: It stops the job from running next time without affecting a job that is already running
It permanently deletes the job from the table
It immediately aborts every running job in Cortex
It converts a time-triggered job into a feed-triggered job
correct_answers: It stops the job from running next time without affecting a job that is already running

questions.question: Which job action starts an aborted or completed job immediately?
options: Run Now
Pause
Disable
Delete
correct_answers: Run Now

questions.question: Which action should be used to halt a running job without deleting it?
options: Pause
Delete
Import
Duplicate
correct_answers: Pause

questions.question: What is a work plan in Cortex?
options: A part of an issue that contains playbooks slated to run for that issue
A global report for all dashboards
A list import wizard
A content pack dependency manifest
correct_answers: A part of an issue that contains playbooks slated to run for that issue

questions.question: Where does the lesson say playbooks for issues can be viewed from the case interface?
options: In the Automation section of the Overview tab on the Cases page
Only in the Marketplace Browse tab
Only in the endpoint inventory table
In the list version history panel
correct_answers: In the Automation section of the Overview tab on the Cases page

questions.question: What is an important consequence of changing the assigned playbook for an event?
options: All completed tasks are removed and the change cannot be undone
All lists are automatically duplicated
The issue is closed immediately
Only failed tasks are removed
correct_answers: All completed tasks are removed and the change cannot be undone

questions.question: What are playbook tasks?
options: The fundamental building blocks that compose playbooks
Static screenshots stored in the Marketplace
Only fields used for license enforcement
Archived job logs that cannot be edited
correct_answers: The fundamental building blocks that compose playbooks

questions.question: Which set contains the four playbook task types described in the lesson?
options: Standard tasks, conditional tasks, data collection, and section headers
Lists, dashboards, reports, and licenses
Issues, cases, assets, and endpoints
Imports, exports, deletes, and downloads
correct_answers: Standard tasks, conditional tasks, data collection, and section headers

questions.question: What does a white diamond on a violet square indicate in a playbook task?
options: Conditional task
Completed task
Failed task
Data collection task
correct_answers: Conditional task

questions.question: What does a small red triangle on a task indicate?
options: The task failed and requires inspection or troubleshooting
The task is a section header
The task is waiting for scheduled execution next week
The task was imported from a local list
correct_answers: The task failed and requires inspection or troubleshooting

questions.question: How do outputs function in a Cortex playbook?
options: They can become inputs for subsequent tasks, creating an interconnected flow
They are discarded before the next task runs
They can only be viewed in the license settings page
They are always converted into HTML templates
correct_answers: They can become inputs for subsequent tasks, creating an interconnected flow

questions.question: Which indicator extraction mode means indicators are not extracted automatically?
options: None
Inline
Out-of-Band
Built-in
correct_answers: None

questions.question: What is the purpose of filters in Cortex?
options: To extract relevant data for further use within the platform
To delete all task outputs after execution
To replace playbook inputs with static screenshots
To disable custom context roots
correct_answers: To extract relevant data for further use within the platform

questions.question: What is a list in Cortex?
options: A container for storing data that is mainly used in playbooks and scripts
A required replacement for every playbook task
A dashboard-only visualization
A type of content pack update
correct_answers: A container for storing data that is mainly used in playbooks and scripts

questions.question: How can a playbook task access data from a list?
options: Through the context button under Lists or with the path ${lists.<list_name>}
Only by exporting the list to PDF
Only by opening the Marketplace Browse tab
By disabling the War Room CLI
correct_answers: Through the context button under Lists or with the path ${lists.<list_name>}

questions.question: Which types of data can be stored in Cortex lists according to the lesson?
options: Text, strings, numbers, Markdown, HTML, CSS, and JSON objects
Only IP addresses
Only screenshots
Only completed job IDs
correct_answers: Text, strings, numbers, Markdown, HTML, CSS, and JSON objects

questions.question: Which list use case helps focus investigations on the most important users or servers?
options: Prioritizing case response with critical asset lists
Deleting all imported threat feeds
Hiding list version history
Converting dashboards into playbooks
correct_answers: Prioritizing case response with critical asset lists

questions.question: Where does the lesson say lists can be created and managed?
options: Settings > Configurations > Object Setup > Lists
Cases & Issues > Case War Room only
Marketplace > Version History
Dashboards > Widgets > Reports
correct_answers: Settings > Configurations > Object Setup > Lists

questions.question: Which option is used to import list items from a local file?
options: The cloud icon at the top right of the Lists page
The playbook brackets icon
The issue severity filter
The table detailed view icon
correct_answers: The cloud icon at the top right of the Lists page

questions.question: Which command creates a new list with a name and list data?
options: createList
getList
setList
removeFromList
correct_answers: createList

questions.question: Which command should be used with the listName argument to retrieve the contents of a list?
options: getList
addToList
setList
createList
correct_answers: getList

questions.question: Which command appends single or multiple items to a specified list?
options: addToList
setList
removeFromList
getList
correct_answers: addToList

questions.question: How can playbook tasks use lists in Cortex?
options: They can automate creating, viewing, and manipulating lists
They can only delete lists after every run
They can use lists only as screenshots
They cannot interact with lists
correct_answers: They can automate creating, viewing, and manipulating lists
